nodes.summary: The graph of an instance $(n, E, K)$ of TOTAL DOMINATING SET is the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E$. Loops are dropped, and pairs with an endpoint at least $n$ contribute no edge.
nodes.title: Graph of a total dominating set instance

nodes.summary: TOTAL DOMINATING SET accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of triples of a natural number, a list of pairs of natural numbers and a natural number, to an instance $(n, E, K)$ that is well formed and feasible: some set of at most $K$ vertices of the graph of the instance contains a neighbor of every vertex. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The decision problem TOTAL DOMINATING SET

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of TOTAL DOMINATING SET is feasible when there is a set $S$ of at most $K$ vertices of its graph such that every vertex $v$ of the graph, including the vertices of $S$, is adjacent to some vertex $u \in S$.
nodes.title: Feasibility of a total dominating set instance

nodes.summary: An instance of TOTAL DOMINATING SET is a triple $(n, E, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edges, and a natural number $K$, the bound.
nodes.title: Instances of TOTAL DOMINATING SET

nodes.summary: The decision problem TOTAL DOMINATING SET belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to TOTAL DOMINATING SET by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: TOTAL DOMINATING SET is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of TOTAL DOMINATING SET is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and its reversal $(v, u)$ does not belong to $E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed total dominating set instances
